Maintainers are responsible for ensuring the system operates efficiently and reliably, addressing any issues that arise during its use. This includes both physical and software maintenance and support. As such, maintainers refers to both software developers and mechanics Unlike passive stakeholders, active stakeholders are deeply involved in the system's day-to- day operations, continuously shaping and adapting its functionality to ensure it meets both immediate and long-term goals. This distinction between active and passive stakeholders is crucial for understanding the system's broader context and ensuring that all interactions, whether direct or indirect, are effectively managed. Concept of Operations The concept of operations depicts how information passes from one component in the system to another. In this concept of operations. The control tablet functions as the main point of operator interaction with the system. All information about the surveyed land is collected by the aerial drone(s) and immediately transferred to the docking drone. The control tablet receives and forwards data from docking drone to the remote server and vice versa. Following this diagram are three scenarios illustrating this concept of operations. Figure 5: Concept of Operations Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory 15 LLNL-TR-2004679 Error reporting When an error is encountered during operations, a timestamp and error code are sent from the affected drone to the user tablet. The tablet then compiles an error report that is sent to the remote server. This report contains timestamps, error codes, all configuration data, and other diagnostic data including temperature, system up-time, and last service date. Maintenance personnel and software developers assess these reports to determine their cause and severity and to recommend solutions Bug fixes If error or diagnostic reports from one or more deployed systems indicate the presence of a software bug, internal software developers will collaborate to find a solution. After enduring QA and being tested on a mock drone setup, the software patch will be pushed to all operator tablets. Each operator will have a week to accept the patch before it runs automatically. At runtime, any applicable updates/patches will be sent from the tablet to the docking drone. The docking drone will forward any applicable updates/patches to all connected aerial drones. Confirmation will then be sent back to the remote server for recording purposes. Scanning for species identification Prior to beginning work, the docking drone requests reference data for the operator selected species. This reference data is stored at the remote server and is delivered to the docking drone through the operator tablet. Once this reference data is loaded locally on the docking drone, the drone swarm begins navigating the working area. The aerial drone(s) takes pictures covering the entire working area. Each picture is sent from the aerial drone(s) to the docking drone, where it is assessed using the downloaded reference data.
